character.name: Clarke Howatt
character.title: Finance Director, Association of Bay Area Governments (ABAG)
character.background: Trusted financial administrator in regional government body
character.motivations: Systematic theft of public housing funds for personal gain

offense.description: Embezzled nearly $3.9 million from the Association of Bay Area Governments between 2011-2015, affecting affordable housing developments including Rincon Hill highrise and Windemere Ranch housing projects
offense.impact: Delayed/compromised affordable housing projects for Bay Area residents

keyFactors: Massive theft from public funds serving vulnerable populations
Court agreed to accept restitution ($3.5M repaid by Howatt and parents)
Restitution strategy led to lenient sentencing despite massive embezzlement
Family money used to mitigate consequences
Minimal prison sentence for stealing nearly $4M from housing fund

consequences: Housing projects delayed for Bay Area residents
Public trust erosion in government financial management
Families needing affordable housing suffered delays
fallout.avoided: Lengthy prison sentence through restitution strategy

narrative_hooks.headline: Finance Director Stole $3.9M from Bay Area Housing Fund, Got 1 Year in Prison
narrative_hooks.question: Why did embezzling $4 million from housing development warrant only 13 months?
narrative_hooks.investigation_angle: The restitution loophole: When money can buy your way out of prison
